title: Communication Efficient and Differentially Private Logistic Regression under the Distributed Setting

problem.claim: Provide differential privacy for logistic regression in a distributed setting.

gap.claim: Prior work has focused mainly on centralized settings with a trusted server, leaving distributed settings less addressed.

contributions.claim: A distributed-setting approach to logistic regression with differential privacy.

narrative_sequence.summary: The paper studies differentially private logistic regression in a distributed setting.
Existing differential privacy research on logistic regression has mostly considered centralized settings with a trusted server.
Distributed scenarios such as federated learning involve clients and servers that may not trust one another.
Clients should provide each local dataset record with a formal privacy guarantee while enabling model learning.

source_observation.claim: Distributed learning may require privacy guarantees for individual records when clients and servers do not mutually trust one another.

interpretation.claim: Privacy requirements should account for both decentralized data ownership and limited trust in infrastructure participants.

application.claim: When designing distributed learning systems, define record-level privacy guarantees across clients and the server.

exception.claim: The supplied abstract units do not specify how the privacy guarantee is implemented or when the lesson applies outside distributed logistic regression.

unknowns: The abstract units do not specify the proposed algorithm.
Communication-efficiency mechanisms and quantitative results are not provided.
Privacy parameters, utility guarantees, and evaluation settings are not provided.
